criteria.title: Analytics Dashboard and EF Core Aggregations
criteria.description: Requirements RPT-01 to RPT-03 work for Admin only (non-Admin receives 403, and without a token 401): GET /admin/dashboard/summary returns the total amount from Succeeded donations only (Sum), their count (Count), the count of distinct donors, and the campaign counts by status Active, Completed, and Expired. GET /admin/dashboard/top-campaigns?count=5 orders by RaisedAmount descending with Take. GET /admin/dashboard/donations-over-time?from=&to= returns daily totals within the range. All reporting queries use AsNoTracking and project directly into DTOs via Select, and AsSplitQuery is used where joined collections exist. The generated SQL (in the log or ToQueryString) actually contains SUM, COUNT, and GROUP BY, with no ToListAsync or AsEnumerable before aggregation (no client-side evaluation).

criteria.title: Dashboard Caching and Matching Database Numbers
criteria.description: RPT-04: Dashboard responses are cached in Redis via IDistributedCache using the cache-aside pattern, with keys that include parameters (count, from, and to), and a default 5-minute expiration configurable via an Options class registered with ValidateOnStart. A hand-written SQL query is included in the README, and when executed, its results match the endpoint numbers (after cache expiration or invalidation). The invalidation strategy and staleness limit are documented in the README.

criteria.title: User and Staff Administration and Its Business Rules
criteria.description: ADM-01: GET /admin/users supports pagination in the unified shape (items, page, pageSize, totalCount, and totalPages), filtering by role, and searching by name or email. ADM-02: PATCH /admin/users/{id}/status activates and deactivates a user, and a deactivated user cannot log in (403 Auth.AccountDeactivated) or refresh tokens. ADM-03: GET /admin/staff, PUT /admin/staff/{id}, and DELETE /admin/staff/{id} work for Admin only on Admin and CampaignManager accounts, and deletion means deactivation rather than hard deletion. An Admin cannot deactivate themself, and the last active Admin cannot be deactivated or deleted. Failures are returned as a Result with error codes from the catalog and mapped to ProblemDetails (no exceptions for business rules). Unit tests cover: blocking self-deactivation, protecting the last active Admin, and preventing a deactivated user from logging in, and all pass in dotnet test.

criteria.title: Multi-Stage Dockerfile
criteria.description: A two-stage Dockerfile exists in the repository root: a build stage based on mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 that copies project files first, runs dotnet restore, copies the remaining source code, and runs dotnet publish -c Release -o /app/publish; and a runtime stage based on mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 that copies only the published artifacts. The image exposes port 8080 and runs as a non-root user (e.g., USER $APP_UID; docker run --entrypoint whoami does not return root). A .dockerignore file excludes bin/, obj/, .git/, and local test results. docker build succeeds without errors.

criteria.title: Docker Compose, Secrets, and Running from a Clean Clone
criteria.description: docker-compose.yml defines the four services: api (built from the local Dockerfile, with all settings from environment variables and depends_on with condition: service_healthy for sqlserver and redis), sqlserver (mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server with a health check and a named volume for data), redis (redis:alpine with a health check), and mailpit (axllent/mailpit on ports 8025 and 1025). A second named volume exists for uploaded files. Intra-network communication uses service names rather than localhost. docker compose up --build brings up all four services without errors, and from a clean clone (after cp .env.example .env) yields a working API with migrations applied and the Admin seeded from SeedAdminOptions. No secrets exist in the repository or its history: .env is in .gitignore, .env.example is committed with placeholder values only, and no secrets are stored in appsettings*.json or docker-compose.yml.

criteria.title: Health Checks
criteria.description: The AspNetCore.HealthChecks.SqlServer and AspNetCore.HealthChecks.Redis packages are installed. /health/live returns 200 without checking any dependencies. /health/ready checks SQL Server, Redis, and write access to the file storage folder via a custom IHealthCheck, returning 503 if any check fails. Both responses are JSON and include each check's name and status. /health/ready is used as the healthcheck for the api service in docker-compose.yml, and the endpoints are not blocked by authentication or rate limiting.

criteria.title: GitHub Actions CI Pipeline
criteria.description: .github/workflows/ci.yml exists and triggers on every push and pull_request across all branches, with steps: actions/checkout, actions/setup-dotnet with version 10.0.x, dotnet restore, dotnet build --no-restore -c Release, and dotnet test --no-build -c Release running unit tests and Sprint 5 integration tests (e.g., against a SQL Server service container). The pipeline fails if the build or any test fails (no continue-on-error). Tests do not call real Stripe or real SMTP, and passwords come from Repository Secrets rather than the workflow file. The CI status badge appears at the top of the README, and the pipeline is passing (green) on the commit tagged sprint-6.

criteria.title: Final README, Architecture Documentation, and Submission
criteria.description: The README contains: the CI badge at the top, an architecture explanation with a diagram, responsibilities of the four layers, vertical slices, and the read/write split, the technology stack and patterns, local run instructions (user-secrets, migrations, and the Redis/Mailpit containers), Docker run instructions (cp .env.example .env then docker compose up), a table of environment variables and Options, local Stripe testing (stripe listen --forward-to, the webhook secret, and stripe trigger), a list of design decisions and their trade-offs (stored RaisedAmount, Result vs. exceptions, idempotency, cache invalidation, soft delete), an endpoint summary and authentication guide, and the SQL query to verify the dashboard. The sprint-6 tag exists, points to the final commit, and has not been moved, and final defense fixes are tagged final.

criteria.title: Explanation of Decisions and Trade-Offs
criteria.description: The learner's ability during code review and final defense preparation to explain the architecture and design patterns and justify the trade-offs in their decisions documented in the README, such as: why reporting queries do not go through the Repository, the difference between AsNoTracking and AsSplitQuery, how to verify that GroupBy was translated to SQL, why RaisedAmount is stored and how to prove its accuracy, how a 5-minute cache aligns with matching database numbers, why the last active Admin is protected even though self-deactivation is blocked, the benefit of a multi-stage Dockerfile and a non-root user, the difference between service_started and service_healthy, the difference between liveness and readiness, where secrets live locally, in Docker, and in CI, and the risks of applying migrations on startup in production. Answers are graded on understanding rather than memorization.
